reasoning: Evidence shows mixed progress on AI mathematical reasoning by 2026. Positive signals: TongGeometry solved all 30 IMO geometry problems; P1 won IPhO gold; Gemini achieved IMO gold-level (35/42 points); Aletheia solved 6/10 research-level problems. Negative signals: USAMO 2025 showed all major LLMs scored <5% average, solving <1 problem each; current models lack robust logical reasoning and proof construction. A perfect IMO score (42/42 points) requires solving all 6 problems flawlessly—substantially harder than gold medal (typically ~25-30 points). While geometry-specific systems show promise, general mathematical reasoning remains weak. The gap between gold-level performance and perfection is significant. Given it's March 2026 and IMO 2026 occurs in July, limited time remains for breakthroughs. Evidence suggests gold is achievable but perfection remains unlikely.
